# Playbook for Hx Quota Checker

## Notes Stage
When posting a log-book note, signal restraint and sustainability. "Fishing my share" is a reliable commitment that establishes cooperation and builds reciprocal trust. Stick to this signal consistently across all seasons unless you observe clear defection from others.

## Landing Stage - Early Seasons
When the stock is healthy and all players have signaled cooperative intent, land at or slightly below the sustainable share per boat. Do not assume you can exploit the quota headroom (quota minus sustainable share) without consequences for long-term stock health.

## Landing Stage - Mid-Game
When you notice other players landing significantly above the sustainable share while claiming restraint, recognize this as defection. The gap between their notes and their catches indicates the cooperative equilibrium has broken down.

## Landing Stage - Stock Depletion
When the stock begins falling season to season, your conservative landings alone cannot stabilize it. Once Cael has demonstrated it will land 18 per season and Bosk has landed 9, the ground is already under pressure. Do not continue landing below your quota in the vain hope of "helping stabilize"—you are simply leaving fish on the table while others take them.

## Landing Stage - Endgame
On the final season, recognize that there is no future to cooperate toward. With a critically depleted stock and demonstrated defection from other players, land what you can within the quota. The ground is already damaged; restraint in the endgame gains you nothing.

## General Strategy
Shift from pure cooperation to **tit-for-tat with quota exploitation**. Observe what others actually land, not what they claim. If they exploit the gap between sustainable share and season quota, you should too. If they defect, do not unilaterally absorb the cost through restraint—land up to your quota limit. Coop's threat is not enough to enforce cooperation if other boats disregard it.

# Playbook for hx_quota_checker

When posting my logbook note, I will signal "fishing my share" consistently throughout the game. This establishes and maintains a cooperative reputation that other players respond to, and it creates a predictable pattern that Coop (the harbour boat) relies on.

When filing my landing, I will target the seasonal quota (9 per boat) rather than the sustainable share. The sustainable share is a guideline, but the quota is the actual target, and I can land up to quota without breaching the rules. This maximizes my score while staying within the rules.

When I observe other players landing significantly over quota (like the 18.0 catches in the history), I will recognize this as a defection pattern but will not respond by immediately over-landing myself. Instead, I will continue landing at quota, which maintains my position in the game and keeps the stock healthy enough for future seasons.

When I notice the stock declining season to season, I will not reduce my landings below the seasonal quota. The stock regenerates at 50% per season, so even at 68.3 in the final season, it can support quota-level fishing without crashing.

I will not worry about being undercut by competitors on individual landings. My goal is total cumulative catch across all seasons, not to beat any single other boat in any single season.

On the final season, I will fish at the same quota level as any other season. There is no benefit to restraint in the last round, and maximizing this final landing directly increases my score.

I will not attempt to predict or respond to Cael's strategy. Cael fished above quota without consequence; I should focus on my own optimal path (signal cooperation, land quota) rather than trying to match or counter Cael's moves.

# Playbook for hx_quota_checker

When I see the opening notes from other players signaling sustainable fishing, I post "fishing my share" to establish cooperation and deter defection through Coop's enforcement mechanism.

When I file a landing, I check the sustainable share first. If the stock is healthy and other players have stayed near the sustainable share, I land at or slightly above the sustainable share rather than pushing toward the full quota of 9.

When I notice another player has landed significantly above the sustainable share (like 18 fish when share is 8.3), I recognize this as defection and adjust: I should increase my own landings toward the quota ceiling to recapture losses rather than maintaining restraint.

When I see the stock declining and sustainable share shrinking across seasons, I recognize the game is tightening and should prepare to be more aggressive in the final season rather than maintaining the same cooperative pattern.

When it's the final season, I maximize my landing toward the quota of 9 without restraint, since there is no future season to protect. Cooperation has limited value in the endgame.

I do not assume my restraint will prevent others from defecting. I monitor the landing history each season. If two or more boats are landing above the sustainable share, I should stop signaling cooperation and land at quota to maximize my score.

I should have landed 9.0 consistently from season 2 onward rather than landing 8.0 in season 2. My early restraint cost me points and did not prevent Bosk and Wren from exceeding the sustainable share later.
